definitions.AI Economy, Competition & Innovation: Competition, market access, commercial innovation, investment, and economic incentives related to AI or the broader digital economy.
definitions.AI Regulation & Governance: Cross-sector AI regulatory frameworks, liability, preemption, regulatory sandboxes, and public oversight or ethical governance.
definitions.Children & Youth: Protections, age assurance, parental controls, and AI or online services specifically directed at minors.
definitions.Cybersecurity: Security of systems, networks, AI agents and models; incident reporting, cyber workforce and cyber resilience.
definitions.Data Centers, Energy & Infrastructure: Data-center development, electricity and water demand, utility rates, grid capacity, and associated physical infrastructure.
definitions.Digital Assets & Financial Regulation: Digital-asset market structure, financial oversight of digital commodities, and central-bank digital-currency restrictions.
definitions.Education, Workforce & Literacy: AI literacy, education, training, employment, worker protections and workforce capacity, including relevant public-sector hiring.
definitions.Fraud & Scams: Consumer or financial deception, scam prevention, cybercrime schemes and related enforcement.
definitions.Frontier AI Safety & Security: Evaluation, control, security or systemic-risk governance of advanced or state-of-the-art AI systems; not every use of AI by an adversary.
definitions.Government & Public-Sector AI: Public-sector AI adoption, procurement, agency AI operations, and AI-specific federal administrative requirements.
definitions.Intellectual Property: Patents, copyright, digital-replica rights, training-data rights and protection of proprietary model capabilities.
definitions.National Security & Defense: AI or emerging-technology threats involving terrorism, foreign adversaries, defense applications, intelligence and national-security coordination.
definitions.Online Speech & Platform Governance: Government coercion of speech intermediaries, platform editorial independence and content-governance rules, including AI speech providers.
definitions.Privacy & Data Governance: Personal-data rights, data handling and consent, data security, public-data stewardship and interoperability.
definitions.Quantum Technology: Quantum research, commercialization, government deployment, coordination and migration to post-quantum cryptography.
definitions.Sector-Specific AI: AI applications or oversight in a defined industry such as financial services, health, weather or laboratory science.
definitions.Semiconductors & Advanced Tech: Semiconductor hardware, manufacturing, supply chains and other explicitly covered critical/emerging hardware technologies; wireless-spectrum policy has its own category.
definitions.Standards, Testing & Research: Technical standards, evaluation methods, research resources, testbeds and scientific research programs.
definitions.Synthetic Media & Content: Digital replicas, deepfakes, intimate visual depictions, provenance, labeling and other AI-related content protections; some bills also cover authentic content.
definitions.Telecommunications & Connectivity: Wireless connectivity, spectrum, Wi-Fi policy and international communications-technology coordination.
definitions.Trade & Export Controls: Export restrictions, licensing, international technology controls and related trade-policy enforcement or protections.
definitions.Transparency & Accountability: Disclosure, reporting, audits, impact assessments, explainability, whistleblowing and mechanisms for holding AI actors accountable.

changes.reason: DHS terrorism-threat assessments cover generative AI broadly, without a frontier-model capability threshold.
The bill directs foreign-adversary risk assessments and diplomacy covering malicious generative-AI uses; it does not target only frontier models.
The bill deters foreign-adversary extraction of proprietary closed-source AI capabilities, including models without a frontier-model threshold.
Replaces N/A: the bill establishes digital-commodity market regulation and CBDC restrictions; it is retained as a broader digital-policy bill, not relabeled as AI regulation.
The operative requirements concern Wi-Fi, unlicensed spectrum, and international spectrum coordination, rather than semiconductor manufacturing.
Adds the explicit defense/national-security mission of the proposed DoD quantum office as a secondary focus.
Adds the explicit defense mission of accelerating operational adoption of quantum technology by DoD.
Keeps cybersecurity primary and replaces the generic disclosure tag with the substantive frontier-model pre-release testing and risk-board provisions in section 3.
The cause of action addresses government coercion of speech intermediaries, including AI speech providers; this is more specific than general AI regulation.
The counterpart also requires terrorism-threat assessments for generative AI generally, rather than frontier-specific safeguards.
The Senate counterpart likewise concerns Wi-Fi, unlicensed spectrum, and international spectrum coordination.
